text:
Ava (infra): quick heads-up — saw SLO drift in eu-west when we kicked a node pool earlier. multi-region failover is fine for availability but latency and cost spiked. want to sketch a playbook for SLA degradation behavior and data-residency-safe fallbacks. thoughts?
Priya (eng-arch): +1. do you mean an automated "degrade" policy or a runbook we trigger manually?
Ava (infra): ideally automated with safe defaults, plus a manual override. automation should avoid moving eu tenants to non-eu unless explicitly allowed.
Mateo (sre): measured impact: tail p95 jumped ~220ms -> 650ms for affected tenants, token cost ~1.6x. root cause was cache warmup + routing to a smaller model variant in another region.
Jun (product): customer question: if we fallback to non-resident region for capacity, do we have consent flow? legal/contract matters for some customers.
Sam (legal): yes — some enterprise contracts require EU-only processing. we need an opt-out flag per tenant and a clear audit log. default must be residency-enforced unless tenant grants opt-in.
Priya (eng-arch): proposal: three-tier fallback policy per tenant: 
1) resident-only: fail closed (reject or queue) 
2) resident-preferred: try resident, if capacity < X, queue for T seconds then serve from resident-shadow or degrade model locally 
3) region-fallback: allow cross-region after explicit opt-in
Mateo (sre): add circuit-breaker thresholds: token-rate, p95-latency, queue-length. if any tripped, trigger staged fallback steps.
Ava (infra): agree. also need KV cache hints so remote region can prewarm. can we expose a client hint to say `X-Resident-Tenant: eu`?
Priya (eng-arch): yes — client hint + async prewarm job. sketch:
```
route_policy: {
  tenant_residency: "eu",
  fallback: "queue_then_fallback",
  queue_ttl_s: 30,
  allowed_regions: ["eu-west1"]
}
```
Mateo (sre): note: prewarm increases cost. we should prewarm only when predicted surge probability > 0.3 (ML model). otherwise cold-start penalty acceptable for low-traffic tenants.
Jun (product): can we add a customer-facing status page flag so customers see when residency is enforced or fallback used? transparency is important.
Sam (legal): audit trail requirement: log every cross-region request with reason. retention 1 year for enterprise customers.
Ava (infra): operational flow idea:
- detection: capacity drop or node eviction in region A
- assessment: runbook checks tenancy residency summary + policy tier
- action: for resident-preferred: queue T=30s, kick prewarm to same region, if fail -> either reject or fallback to variant (quantized or smaller model) in region A or fallback to approved region B if opt-in
- postmortem: auto-create incident with metrics snapshot
OpsBot: incident INC-3421 created (auto) for cluster eu-west evict, linked to this thread.
Priya (eng-arch): edge cases: long-running sessions with large KV caches — migrating is expensive. maybe keep session sticky to original region if data residency allows, otherwise tear down session with clear client message.
Mateo (sre): agree — add graceful teardown: 1) notify client with header `x-reason: region-evacuation`, 2) allow 60s to checkpoint, 3) close session.
Jun (product): ui wording proposal for SDKs: "We’re experiencing temporary service disruptions in your region. Requests may be delayed or routed to an alternate region if you opted in."
Sam (legal): ok with wording, but require explicit opt-in phrase for cross-region. store timestamped consent.
Ava (infra): action items: Priya to draft route policy schema + API flag, Mateo to add circuit-breaker thresholds and incident automation, Jun to draft customer messaging, Sam to add contract language snippet. I'll prototype a prewarm lambda.
Priya (eng-arch): I'll put a short RFC up today with policy examples and API changes — ping @Ava for review.
Mateo (sre): I'll add quick dashboards: queue length, prewarm success rate, cross-region served count.
Jun (product): I'll write the SDK message strings and status page stub.
Sam (legal): I'll circulate contract excerpt for residency opt-in consent.
Ava (infra): thanks — if no objections I'll start prototyping tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Priya (eng-arch): +1
Mateo (sre): +1
Jun (product): +1
Sam (legal): +1
